newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria says it wants to be a full NATO member.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria says it wants to be a full NATO member.

text.p: Bulgaria's caretaker government on Monday adopted a declaration stating its desire for full NATO membership in an effort to clarify the country's policy, Foreign Minister Stoyan Stalev said.
"The cabinet adopted a declaration in which it clearly states its will for full NATO membership," Stalev told reporters.

The declaration, endorsed by Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov, aims to qualify the Balkan country for membership nomination at a NATO summit in July, where the alliance will decide which new members to admit.
"We would not like to let our economic crisis hinder development of foreign policy," said Stalev.
"We would like to have our membership candidacy considered on an equal footing as those of other east European countries," he added.

Reform-laggard Bulgaria has fallen behind top contenders in the race for memebership such as Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, although like most ex-communist states, it takes part in NATO's Partnership for Peace initiative designed to foster cooperation between former Cold War foes.
In the declaration, shortly to be presented to NATO headquarters, Bulgaria states its will to be invited to accession talks, Stalev said.

U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright undertook an 11-day trip to nine world capitals on NATO expansion plans and to persuade Russia to agree by the July summit on a charter defining a special relationship with the alliance.

Despite a 1993 parliamentary declaration stating Bulgaria's desire to join the alliance, the ruling Socialists have fudged the issue over the past two years because of traditionally warm ties with Russia, which strongly opposes NATO's eastward expansion.

The Socialists stepped down from power two weeks ago and 20 months before the end of their term, bowing to opposition demands for early elections after 30 days of mass protests fuelled by economic hardship.

President Petar Stoyanov, elected on the opposition ticket in November, stated Bulgaria's clear intention to join the alliance immediately after taking office in January during a visit to NATO headquarters in Brussels.
The opposition Union of Democratic Forces, the favorite to win general elections on April 19, has traditionally supported Bulgaria's bid to join the North Atlalntic Treaty Organisation.
Bulgaria's foreign ministry is expected to work out a NATO accession plan, which would include evaluation of the country's capacity to adjust to the standards of the alliance.
Stalev said the current government will immediately begin lobbying with NATO members.
